messages.subject: Adding a common formatting line to my knitted PDF files
messages.subject_clean: Adding a common formatting line to my knitted PDF files
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I have been experimenting with more Rmarkdown and Rmd.  I am running into a bit of trouble with the PDF files.  They look fine on the screen, but when I print them, the font size is very small.

If I enter the line "font size: 12pt", into the output options.

But I thought I would put together an _output.yaml file to contain that for PDF documents.  That didn't work at all.

Is there a work-around for this, or should I just suck it up and enter my line?  Sometimes I like to change the figure size too.

This is R Version 3.2.2, Mac, Rstudio 0.99.473

Thanks,
Erin

messages.subject_clean: Adding a common formatting line to my knitted PDF files
messages.body_plain:
Woo hoo!

I figured it out at last.  Just in case anyone cares (a set of measure zero!) this is what I have:

title: "Review of Stat I Concepts Part 1"
output: pdf_document
fontsize: 12pt
geometry: margin=1in
documentclass: article
classoption: fleqn

And everything works like a charm!

Thanks,
Erin

Hi Michael and everyone:

When I tried using the _output.yaml file, it simply did not work for me.  I'm guess that I did something wrong.

So what I do now:
a.  Put together all of my stuff
b.  knit my HTML  (those changes don't impact the HTML)
c.  Then edit the output to pdf_document and add the material as mentioned
d.  knit my PDF

The PDF then has the correct size for printing.

Thanks for listening/reading.

PS.  I really did laugh out loud when I saw your "measure zero" metric!

messages.subject: Trying to produce rotations in an HTML file via the Rmarkdown knit HTML
messages.subject_clean: Trying to produce rotations in an HTML file via the Rmarkdown knit HTML
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I am trying to produce a 3d plot in rgl within Rmarkdown.  I have set up x, y, and z vectors, and produced a persp3d plot.  Then I used the writeWebGL function, and put the same file name as the output file.  I was hoping that the plot would appear in the HTML page, and that I would still be able to rotate that plot.

Here is the code:

---
title: "test for rotations"
date: "September 14, 2015"
output: html_document
---

Test 1

```{r}
x <- 1:5/10
y <- 1:5
z <- x %o% y
z <- z + .2*z*runif(25) - .1*z
# Bring in the 3d library
library(rgl)
# Plot the structure
persp3d(x, y, z, col="skyblue")
# write to an HTML file
writeWebGL(dir="/Users/emhodgess",file="/Users/emhodgess/testrgl1.html",template = system.file(file.path("WebGL", "template.html"), package = "rgl"),
           reuse=TRUE)
```

I'm also attaching the file itself.  Including "no fun" final html file as well.

Thank you so much in advance for any help.

Sincerely,
Erin
Note:  R Version 3.2.2, on a Mac.

messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Trying to produce rotations in an HTML file via the Rmarkdown knit HTML
messages.body_plain:
You can just use the hook function hook_webgl() in rgl, e.g.

---
title: "test for rotations"
date: "September 14, 2015"
output: html_document
---

Test 1

```{r}

library(rgl)
knitr::knit_hooks$set(webgl = hook_webgl)
```

```{r webgl=TRUE}

x <- 1:5/10
y <- 1:5
z <- x %o% y
z <- z + .2*z*runif(25) - .1*z
# Bring in the 3d library
library(rgl)
# Plot the structure
persp3d(x, y, z, col="skyblue")

```

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name
